dedupe_keys.name: cost benefit analysis of cycle superhighways with e bikes in greater copenhagen

description: This case study by Jeppe Rich, Anders Fjendbo Jensen, Ninette Pilegaard and Martin Hallberg of the Technical University of Denmark (Case Studies on Transport Policy, 2021) carries out a cost-benefit analysis of an ambitious cycle superhighway network in the Greater Copenhagen area. Coverage: the proposed regional network, with the effects of electric and conventional bikes separated so that travel time savings reflect different speed profiles and the external health and safety effects differ by bicycle technology. The network has a positive net present value, with an internal rate of return between 6% and 23% depending on the assumptions, which the authors say exceeds other network infrastructure that is often prioritised. Larger shares of e-bikes lower the benefits, because e-bikes bring smaller health gains and larger accident costs that outweigh their extra travel time savings, and most benefits accrue outside the municipality that builds the route. Format and access: a journal article. Licence and cost: the article is closed and the abstract is public. Caveats: results depend on assumed demand and unit values; the model and inputs are not published with the paper. The appraisal structure can be used to set benefit parameters when simulating cycling network investments or mode shift scenarios. It relates to the WHO HEAT tool and the Bicycle Network Analysis in the catalogue.
